title: Data Types Quiz
description: Review integers, floats, booleans, strings, None, truthiness, and the type() function.

questions.explanation: A decimal point makes the literal a float, not an int.
type() returns the class object representing the value's type.

questions.prompt: In Python, `True` and `False` are boolean values.
questions.explanation: bool is the type for logical true and false; the literals are capitalized True and False.
Zero, empty containers, None, and empty strings are falsy in boolean context.
An empty string is falsy, so bool('') is False.
None is its own type (NoneType) representing absence of a value.
Quotes create str literals; unquoted numbers and booleans are other types.
Empty sequences and collections evaluate to False in if statements and bool().
The / operator always returns a float in Python 3, even when the result is whole.
None belongs to the NoneType class.
Non-empty strings are truthy, including the string '0'.
isinstance checks whether an object is an instance of a given type.
int() truncates toward zero; it does not round to the nearest integer.

questions.prompt: Which pair has the same type?
questions.explanation: Both 3 and 99 are int literals.
None is falsy.

questions.prompt: Strings are immutable. What does that mean?
options: You cannot change characters in place; create a new string instead
Strings cannot be stored in variables
str is not a built-in type
questions.explanation: Methods like .upper() return new strings rather than modifying the original.

questions.prompt: Every object in Python has a type.
questions.explanation: All values are objects, and type() or isinstance can identify their class.
float() converts integers to floating-point numbers.

questions.prompt: Which best describes Python's dynamic typing?
options: A variable can refer to values of different types over time
Types are chosen at compile time only
All variables must be declared as int or str
Types cannot be inspected at runtime
questions.explanation: Names are not permanently tied to one type; assignment can change what type a name refers to.
Quotes make '3' a string, not the integer 3.
